_meta.purpose: One entry per GitHub issue: what changed, where, how it was checked and what is left. Read this before starting an issue; update it in the same pull request that does the work.

status_values.in_progress: Someone is working on it; assignee and branch are set
status_values.on_hold: Do not start until the on-hold label is removed
status_values.in_review: Work is in an open pull request
status_values.ready_for_review: Implemented and verified on a feature branch; not merged

how_to_update: Starting an issue: set status to in_progress, fill assignee and branch, and assign yourself on GitHub
Finishing: set status to done, fill commit (hash, date, message, files), changes, verification and deviations_from_issue
Changing something a finished issue built: add an entry to that issue's revisions with the commit and a one-line summary
Work that belongs to no single issue goes in other_changes
Anything the next person must know goes in follow_ups
After a batch of work, add a dated record to the top of entries, including anything changed outside the repo and anything not verified

sections.entries: Dated records of a batch of work, newest first: what changed, the numbers that moved, changes made outside the repo, what was and was not verified
sections.issues: Current state of every GitHub issue
sections.other_changes: Work that belongs to no single issue

Added one-step Undo for the most recent response choice. It restores the prior decision or Needs review state and any prior rejection note without discarding other shipments' changes.

Added Normal-scenario guidance and collapsible empty groups on small screens. Selected shipments expose a View responses shortcut; Back to shipments restores queue focus.
Kept horizontal scrolling inside the comparison table on mobile so its shipment context and confirmation notices remain fully visible.
Changed the starting and Reset scenario to Disrupted at the user's request. Reset clears decisions, previews, Undo and empty-group disclosure; Normal remains available.
Separated Reject all from the selected shipment outline with 8px of vertical spacing so its border and keyboard focus ring are not cut off.

After the final border and mobile-scroll fixes, reran lint, production build (including typecheck) and all 74 tests in the four affected UI test files; all passed.

notes: Recorded on Nicole's feature branch; no pull request has been opened or merged.
The Disrupted starting/Reset scenario intentionally supersedes the earlier Normal default; the user explicitly chose the matching Reset behavior.

Historical route comparison remains on hold; no new dependencies, calculations or route rankings were introduced.

entries.title: Sanity checks for the corridor data, the map layers and the truck record
entries.summary: Seventeen new checks guard the G3 to G5 work against future changes: the generated data files must agree with each other and with the scripts that write them, the community counts must match everywhere they are shown, and the pipeline must keep running the whole suite.

commits.message: Add sanity checks for the corridor data, map layers and truck record

checks: Data (12 checks, new file sanity/data.sanity.test.ts): the projection and the 150 m distance tests give known values; every script table covers every segment; each script is named in the data README; the corridor analysis matches the current segment lines; reapplying the stored analysis changes no file; each place is counted once per route; the map's layers hold exactly the counted places; Caltrans records point at segments that exist; simulated files stay SIMULATED; real layers keep their label, publisher, edition, address and date; no note says a route is legal, safe or suitable for trucks

Browser (3 new, 9 in all): community counts match between the comparison table and the map panel and follow a previewed reroute; the truck network row is shown as a record with no verdict; the real map draws one graphic per counted school and tract

Pipeline (2 new, 11 repository checks in all): the workflow runs lint, typecheck, tests, build and the sanity suite on pull requests into staging and main and has a browser and Python; every test file in sanity/ matches the pattern the suite runs
pipeline: The sanity job already runs every file matching sanity/**/*.sanity.test.ts, so the new checks run there with no new job
Added a step that prints the Python version before the build, so a runner without python3 fails with a clear message instead of inside a check

decisions: The data checks import the Python scripts and run their pure functions; they never call the downloads, so the pipeline needs no network access to Caltrans, NCES, OEHHA or the feature service
Expected counts in the browser checks are read from src/data, so rerunning the corridor analysis does not break them
verification: npm run sanity passes: 45 checks in 5 files; npm test passes (195 tests); typecheck and lint pass
Each of three deliberate breaks was caught and then undone: a count edited by hand in routes.json, a segment line moved, and a school removed from the map layers
Locally the real map started in headless Chromium and drew 9 schools and 31 tracts for R-A-ALT, matching the data
not_verified: The workflow change has not run on GitHub: the branch is not pushed and no pull request is open
On a runner with no WebGL the drawn-places check reports that it was skipped instead of failing, as the existing map check does
known_gaps: scripts/import_map_data.py against the live feature service is still not checked: it needs the network, and it currently fails on the extended service
The downloads in the corridor and reference-data scripts are not exercised

entries.title: Added sanity checks and a pipeline job that runs them
entries.summary: A new suite checks that the project as a whole still works: the repository, this change log, the production build, and the built app driven through its main flow in a real browser. The pipeline runs it on every pull request and push to main and staging.

commits.message: Add sanity checks and run them in the pipeline

checks: Repository (9 checks): npm scripts named in the README and workflows, README layout, valid Python in scripts/, no tracked .env, keys or build output, .env.example has names only, browser code reads only VITE_ variables

Change log (9 checks): sections, dates newest first, unique issue numbers and codes, known statuses, summary counts match, worked-on issues have an assignee, branch, commit, changes and verification, references resolve, listed files still exist

Build (4 checks): page has its root and title, every script and stylesheet it loads exists, the ArcGIS map is one separate chunk and first-load JavaScript is under 500 kB, no server-side variable names in the bundle

Browser (6 checks): starts with no errors and one card per shipment, the closure moves the affected shipments to Needs review, the reference shipment shows Wait, Reroute and Request later slot, every shipment opens in both scenarios, Reset clears everything, the real map chunk loads and the view starts cleanly where it can
pipeline: Job 'Sanity checks on the built app' added to .github/workflows/advisory-checks.yml: npm ci, install headless Chromium, npm run build, npm run test:sanity
The workflow itself was added in 9511f83 and had no change log record until now
project: package.json: scripts test:sanity and sanity; dev dependency playwright 1.65.0
vitest.sanity.config.ts keeps the sanity checks out of npm test; tsconfig.sanity.json and eslint.config.js cover sanity/
README: a Sanity checks section and the sanity/ folder in the layout
change_log: summary.pull_requests: #26 marked merged into staging (4296815); #27 (staging to main) added
G2 (#20) follow_ups: the map fallback gap described under known_gaps

decisions: The browser values are read from src/data, so refreshing the data from the feature service does not break the checks

The dashboard checks hold the map chunk back: without WebGL the SDK throws an uncaught error, which would fail them on a runner with no graphics. This also exercises the pane's fallback in a real browser
One check loads the real map. Where the browser has WebGL and reaches Esri, the view must start with no uncaught errors; otherwise the check passes with a warning that the view was not checked
scripts/import_map_data.py --check is not in the pipeline: it depends on the live feature service, which anyone can edit, so it would fail unrelated pull requests
verification: npm run sanity: 28 of 28 checks pass locally (macOS, Node 24, headless Chromium), in about 8 seconds after the build
npm run lint, typecheck and test pass (84 unit tests, unchanged)
The real map view started in headless Chromium with no uncaught errors

Checks fail when they should, each tried and then undone: a wrong count in this file, a listed file renamed, a server-side variable read in src, a missing npm script named in the README, the map imported without lazy loading, a crash on one shipment
With WebGL turned off in the browser, all six browser checks still pass and the map check prints its warning
not_verified: The new job has not run on GitHub: the commit is local and has not been pushed
Whether the map view starts on GitHub's Linux runner. The browser is started with software WebGL allowed, but this was only tried on macOS
Docker was not running, so the checks were not tried in a Linux container
known_gaps: Map fallback: with no WebGL, or with Esri's servers unreachable, the map view never starts and the pane does not show 'The map could not load'; that message only appears when the map chunk fails to load. Without WebGL the SDK also throws an uncaught error. Not fixed here; noted on G2 (#20)
The change log check on listed files will fail a pull request that removes or renames a file without listing the old path under deleted
The key scan looks for a few common key formats; it is not a full secret scanner
Issues #19 and #20 stay in_review until staging reaches main
